description: Twenty-panel bright-field TEM montage (a–t) of deformation-induced microstructure in a Fe35Mn6Al0.1C low-density cryogenic steel tensile-tested at liquid nitrogen temperature (LNT), each panel stamped with its engineering strain: (a,b) 3 %, (c–e) 10 %, (f–i) 20 %, (j–o) 28 %, (p,q) 38 %, (r–t) 55 %. Every panel is a TEM micrograph with a printed 200 nm, 500 nm or 1 µm scale bar, and most carry a green-circled SAED inset. (a) labels dislocation nodes, dislocation pairs and dislocation multi-junctions; (b) shows a {111}-faceted boundary with a circled "MC" particle and an inset annotated "Stacking fault" (dashed arrows on the fringes). (d) and (h) show thin deformation twins (dashed circles) nucleated at annealed twin boundaries; (e) prints twin bundle "Width≈5 nm" at 10 % and (i) "Width≈24nm" at 20 %. (f) is annotated "Cell blocks" and (g) "Dislocation cells" with a double-headed "TA" (tensile axis) arrow. (j) shows deformation twins plus cell blocks; (k) prints "Width≈157nm", (l) labels "Microbands" at a "GB" with "Width≈390nm", and (n) prints "Microbands Width≈137nm". (p,q) show dense primary twin bundles at 38 %; (r) separates "Primary twins" from "Secondary twins" at 55 %, and (t), a 10 nm-bar lattice image, shows secondary twins rich in stacking faults. The group argues that deformation twinning nucleates at annealed twin boundaries via stacking faults and progressively replaces planar slip.

observations.observation: Each of the 20 TEM panels carries a strain label printed in its corner: 3 % for (a,b), 10 % for (c–e), 20 % for (f–i), 28 % for (j–o), 38 % for (p,q) and 55 % for (r–t).
Panel (a) (3 %) is annotated with the regions 'Dislocation nodes', 'Dislocation pairs' and 'Dislocation multi-junctions'.
Panel (b) (3 %) contains an inset annotated 'Stacking fault' with dashed arrows marking the fringe contrast, and a circled particle labelled 'MC' near a {111} boundary trace.
Printed width measurements in the panels are: 'Width≈5 nm' (e, 10 %), 'Width≈24nm' (i, 20 %), 'Width≈390nm' (l, 28 %), 'Width≈157nm' (k, 28 %) and 'Microbands Width≈137nm' (n, 28 %).
Panel (l) shows microbands originating at a grain boundary (labelled 'GB') while panel (n) shows microbands within the grain interior, both highlighted by green circles.
Panel (f) is annotated 'Cell blocks' and panel (g) 'Dislocation cells', the latter with a double-headed arrow labelled 'TA' indicating the tensile axis direction.
Panel (r) (55 %) distinguishes 'Primary twins' from 'Secondary twins', and panel (t) is a 10 nm-scale-bar lattice image of heavily faulted twin lamellae.
Most panels include a selected-area electron diffraction inset, typically showing a single-crystal spot pattern with four reflections circled in green; the (r) inset shows streaked spots.
The caption states the panels are TEM images of deformation-induced microstructure at different tensile strains at LNT, indicating the occurrence of deformation twins at 10 % tensile strain.

The citing text states that at 3 % strain complex planar slip features, dislocation pairs, nodes and multiple dislocations emerged, and that extended dislocation pairs at low temperature indicate low temperature facilitates planar glide.

The citing text states that stacking faults formed at annealed twin boundaries at 3 % strain (Fig. 8(b) inset) and that deformation twins nucleated at those boundaries at about 10 % strain, with a twin bundle width of about 5 nm that cannot be detected by EBSD.
The citing text states that broad microbands reach widths of approximately 390 nm and fine microbands about 137 nm, the broad ones originating from grain boundaries and the fine ones within grains.

The citing text attributes the nearly constant strain-hardening rate at LNT to twin activation at annealed twin boundaries seeded by pre-existing stacking faults, and rejects a Taylor-lattice explanation because cross-slip is enhanced in this steel.

The citing text assigns cell blocks to panel (e) and dislocation cells to panel (g), whereas the panel labels place the 5 nm twin-width measurement in (e) at 10 % and 'Cell blocks' in (f) at 20 %; the panel-to-text mapping appears inconsistent in the citing text.
